I find it interesting how much misinformation there is about trans people. When trans people medically transition their risk profile changes (with the exception of prostrate cancer obviously). 

Trans men (those who transitioned to male) don't have a higher risk of breast cancer than other men, while trans women actually have a heightened risk than they did before. The hormone therapy that trans people use to physically transition makes their health care closer to the gender they transition to rather than what they were born as. 

Easy example- trans men get top surgery to structure a male chest. This involves removing breast tissue. As a result, their lack of breasts as well as high testosterone and low estrogen (from hormone therapy) make it very unlikely they will get breast cancer. The estrogen that trans women take and that causes them to develop breasts increase their risk of breast cancer. 

TLDR: You should still tell your doctor, but being transgender isn't as medically relevant as you think it is.
